prompt: A company has no on-premises Active Directory and keeps all identities in Microsoft Entra ID. It is buying new corporate-owned Windows 11 laptops and wants users to sign in to Windows with their work accounts and get single sign-on to Microsoft 365. Which device identity should the administrator plan for the laptops?

options.text: Microsoft Entra registered
Microsoft Entra hybrid joined
Microsoft Entra joined
Active Directory domain joined and synchronized with Microsoft Entra Connect

explanation: Microsoft Entra join is designed for organization-owned devices in cloud-first or cloud-only organizations, with the work account as the Windows sign-in. Microsoft Entra registered is meant for personal (BYOD) devices where the user keeps a personal sign-in. Microsoft Entra hybrid joined and Active Directory domain joined both require an on-premises Active Directory domain, which this company doesn't have.

prompt: Employees want to use their personal Windows 11 PCs to reach Microsoft 365 resources. They want to keep signing in to Windows with their personal Microsoft accounts. The organization still needs the devices to have an identity in Microsoft Entra ID so that Conditional Access can evaluate them. Which approach should the administrator plan?

options.text: Microsoft Entra registration by adding a work or school account
Microsoft Entra hybrid join through Microsoft Entra Connect
Microsoft Entra join during the out-of-box experience
Windows Autopilot self-deploying mode

explanation: Microsoft Entra registration (adding a work or school account) gives a personal device an identity in Microsoft Entra ID, and the user keeps signing in with a personal account. Microsoft Entra join makes the work account the device sign-in and is intended for corporate devices. Hybrid join requires the device to be joined to on-premises Active Directory, and Autopilot self-deploying mode is for corporate devices with no user affinity.

prompt: An organization has thousands of Windows devices joined to its on-premises Active Directory domain. They depend on existing Group Policy objects. The security team now wants Conditional Access to recognise these devices without rejoining them to a different directory. What should the administrator implement?

options.text: Microsoft Entra registration on each device by the users
Reset each device and Microsoft Entra join it with Windows Autopilot
Enterprise State Roaming for all users
Microsoft Entra hybrid join configured through Microsoft Entra Connect

explanation: Microsoft Entra hybrid join keeps devices joined to on-premises Active Directory, so Group Policy keeps working, and also registers them in Microsoft Entra ID for Conditional Access. Having users register domain-joined devices is not the supported way to give them a corporate device identity. Resetting and Entra joining every device contradicts the requirement to keep the existing join. Enterprise State Roaming syncs user settings and creates no device identities.

prompt: A company plans to Microsoft Entra join all new Windows devices. Users still need single sign-on to on-premises file servers that use Kerberos authentication. Which condition must be true for the users to get that single sign-on from the Microsoft Entra joined devices?

options.text: The devices must also be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined to the domain.
Users must be hybrid identities synced from on-premises Active Directory.
The devices must be Microsoft Entra registered instead of joined.
Device writeback must be enabled in Microsoft Entra Connect.

explanation: Microsoft Entra joined devices can give single sign-on to on-premises resources when the user is a hybrid identity synchronized from Active Directory and the device has line of sight to a domain controller. A device can't be both Entra joined and hybrid joined, and hybrid join isn't required for this. Registration doesn't give a Windows sign-in with the work account. Device writeback isn't a requirement for Kerberos single sign-on from Entra joined devices.

prompt: Only members of the IT deployment team should be able to Microsoft Entra join Windows devices. Everyone else must be blocked from joining devices. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An Intune device limit restriction set to zero for all other users
Assign the Cloud Device Administrator role to the deployment team members
A Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device for all cloud apps
Set 'Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra' to Selected with the team's group

explanation: The device setting 'Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra' can be set to Selected so that only the chosen users or groups can join devices. An Intune device limit restriction controls Intune enrollment counts, not who can join devices to the directory. Giving the team a role doesn't stop other users from joining. A compliant-device Conditional Access policy controls access to apps, not the ability to join devices.

prompt: The help desk team needs local administrator rights on every Microsoft Entra joined Windows device in the tenant. The team shouldn't receive broader directory privileges. Which Microsoft Entra role should the administrator assign to the team?

options.text: Cloud Device Administrator
Microsoft Entra Joined Device Local Administrator
Intune Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator

explanation: Members of the Microsoft Entra Joined Device Local Administrator role are added to the local Administrators group on all Microsoft Entra joined devices. Cloud Device Administrator manages device objects in the directory (enable, disable, delete) but doesn't grant local administrator rights on devices. Intune Administrator is a broad service role, and Helpdesk Administrator resets passwords for non-admin users. Neither gives local administrator rights.

prompt: An administrator wants a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication at the moment a user joins or registers a device with Microsoft Entra ID, not at every app sign-in. What should the policy target?

options.text: The user action 'Register or join devices'
The Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app
All cloud apps, with the grant control set to require multifactor authentication
All cloud apps, with the grant control set to require a device marked as compliant

explanation: Conditional Access can target the user action 'Register or join devices', which applies the requirement only when a device is registered or joined. When you use this approach, set the device setting that requires MFA to register or join devices to No. The Microsoft Intune Enrollment app covers Intune enrollment, not directory registration. Targeting all cloud apps would prompt at every app sign-in, and a compliant-device grant doesn't require MFA at all.

prompt: A user wants to register a personal Windows 11 PC with Microsoft Entra ID and keep their existing local sign-in. Which action should the user take on the device?

options.text: Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Join this device to Microsoft Entra ID
System Properties > Computer Name > Change, then enter the company domain
Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Connect, then sign in with the work account
Settings > Accounts > Email & accounts > Add a Microsoft account

explanation: Selecting Connect under Access work or school and signing in with a work account registers the device, and the user's existing sign-in doesn't change. 'Join this device to Microsoft Entra ID' performs a Microsoft Entra join, which makes the work account the device sign-in. Changing the domain in System Properties joins an on-premises domain. Adding a Microsoft account adds a personal consumer account and doesn't register the device with the organization.

prompt: A long-time employee gets an error saying they have reached the maximum number of devices when they try to register a new device with Microsoft Entra ID. The tenant uses the default device settings. Most of the user's existing device objects haven't signed in for over a year. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Raise the user's limit in the Intune device limit enrollment restriction
Delete the user's stale device objects in Microsoft Entra ID
Assign the user a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
Enable Enterprise State Roaming for the user

explanation: The Microsoft Entra device setting 'Maximum number of devices per user' limits how many joined or registered devices a user can have (50 by default). Removing stale device objects frees up space under that limit. The Intune device limit restriction applies to Intune enrollment, not directory registration. A P2 license doesn't raise this limit. Enterprise State Roaming is unrelated to device registration.

prompt: Personal Windows devices are Microsoft Entra registered but not enrolled in Intune. A Conditional Access policy that requires a device marked as compliant blocks these devices from SharePoint Online. Management wants the devices to get access when they meet the organization's security requirements. What should happen?

options.text: Convert the devices to Microsoft Entra hybrid joined
Set 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' to Compliant
Assign the users Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses
Enroll the devices in Intune and assign a compliance policy to them

explanation: A device only gets a compliance state when an MDM service such as Intune manages it and evaluates a compliance policy. Registration alone doesn't produce a compliance state. Hybrid join needs on-premises domain membership, which personal devices don't have. The 'no compliance policy assigned' setting only applies to enrolled devices. The P2 license doesn't change how compliance is evaluated.

prompt: An administrator needs a dynamic device group that automatically contains every device registered with Windows Autopilot, whatever its group tag or profile. Which membership rule should be used?

options.text: (device.deviceOSType -eq "Windows")
(device.enrollmentProfileName -eq "Autopilot")
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -startsWith "[ZTDid]"))
(device.deviceOwnership -eq "Company")

explanation: Autopilot-registered devices carry a ZTDId value in devicePhysicalIds, so a rule that checks for the [ZTDid] prefix captures all of them. A rule on deviceOSType Windows includes every Windows device, Autopilot or not. enrollmentProfileName matches a single named profile, not all Autopilot devices. deviceOwnership Company includes any corporate device, whether or not it is registered with Autopilot.

prompt: Autopilot devices for the sales department are imported with the group tag Sales. The administrator wants a dynamic device group that contains only those devices so that a sales-specific Autopilot profile can be assigned. Which rule should be used?

options.text: (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:Sales"))
(device.displayName -startsWith "Sales")
(user.department -eq "Sales")
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -startsWith "[ZTDid]"))

explanation: An Autopilot group tag is stored in devicePhysicalIds as an OrderID entry, so matching [OrderID]:Sales selects exactly those devices. A displayName rule depends on device names, which may not be set yet when the profile must be assigned. A user.department rule is a user attribute and can't be combined with device rules in a device group. The ZTDid rule matches all Autopilot devices, not just sales devices.

prompt: An administrator tries to create a security group and finds that the Dynamic Device membership type isn't available. The tenant currently has only the Microsoft Entra ID Free edition. What must be in place to use dynamic membership rules?

options.text: The Groups Administrator role for the administrator
Intune Plan 2 licensing
Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or a plan that includes it) licensing for the tenant
The group type set to Microsoft 365 instead of Security

explanation: Dynamic membership groups require Microsoft Entra ID P1 licensing, which is also included in P2 and in suites such as Microsoft 365 E3. A Groups Administrator who has the licence can manage dynamic groups, but the role doesn't remove the licensing requirement. Intune Plan 2 doesn't provide Entra dynamic groups. Changing to a Microsoft 365 group doesn't avoid the licence requirement, and dynamic device membership applies only to security groups.

prompt: An administrator is preparing the device group that a Windows Autopilot device preparation policy will use, so that devices are added to the group during enrollment. How should the group be created?

options.text: As an assigned security group with the Intune Provisioning Client service principal as an owner
As a dynamic device security group whose rule matches the [ZTDid] prefix
As a Microsoft 365 group with the deployment team as owners
As a dynamic user group that contains the users who will set up the devices

explanation: Enrollment time grouping needs a static (assigned) Microsoft Entra security group, and the Intune Provisioning Client service principal must be one of its owners so that Intune can add devices during enrollment. Dynamic groups aren't used for this, because the point is to avoid waiting for dynamic membership evaluation. A Microsoft 365 group or a user group isn't the device security group the policy requires.

prompt: Shared iPads are enrolled through Apple automated device enrollment with an enrollment profile named Kiosk-iPads. The administrator wants a dynamic device group that automatically contains every iPad enrolled with that profile. Which rule should be used?

options.text: (device.deviceModel -eq "iPad")
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:Kiosk-iPads"))
(device.deviceOSType -eq "iPad")
(device.enrollmentProfileName -eq "Kiosk-iPads")

explanation: Devices enrolled through an Apple automated device enrollment profile report the profile name in enrollmentProfileName, so the rule captures only iPads that used Kiosk-iPads. Model-based and OS-type-based rules would also include iPads enrolled in other ways. The OrderID entry holds Autopilot group tags for Windows devices and isn't populated from Apple enrollment profiles.

prompt: Users Microsoft Entra join new Windows 11 devices during the out-of-box experience, but the devices never show up in Intune. Microsoft Entra ID P1 and Intune licences are assigned. What should the administrator configure so that these devices enroll automatically?

options.text: Set only the MAM user scope to All
Set the Microsoft Intune MDM user scope to include the users (Some or All)
Create a device platform restriction that allows Windows (MDM)
Configure Windows Hello for Business as a tenant-wide enrollment setting

explanation: Windows automatic enrollment happens when the user who joins the device is within the MDM user scope configured for Microsoft Intune. The MAM user scope is for app protection without enrollment and doesn't enroll devices in MDM. Platform restrictions can only block enrollments that are already being attempted, and Windows Hello for Business settings don't trigger enrollment.

prompt: A device platform restriction blocks personally owned Windows devices from enrolling. Some corporate laptops that IT enrolls manually with the Settings app are now blocked as personal devices. The company has the serial number, manufacturer and model of each laptop. What should the administrator do so that these laptops enroll as corporate without changing the restriction?

options.text: Increase the device limit in the default device limit restriction
Assign the laptops a device category
Set the laptops' ownership to Corporate after enrollment
Add the laptops' details as corporate device identifiers in Intune

explanation: Uploading Windows corporate identifiers (serial number, manufacturer and model) lets Intune treat matching devices as corporate during enrollment, so the personal-device block doesn't apply to them. The device limit restriction controls how many devices a user can enroll, not ownership. Device categories are only labels for grouping. Changing ownership after enrollment is too late because the block happens during enrollment.

prompt: Employees want their personal iPhones to access corporate apps. They require that IT can't see personal apps or wipe the whole device, and corporate data must be kept separate. The organization uses Managed Apple Accounts. Which enrollment method should the administrator configure?

options.text: Automated device enrollment through Apple Business Manager
Account-driven User Enrollment
Device enrollment with the Company Portal app
Apple Configurator enrollment

explanation: Account-driven User Enrollment is designed for personal devices. It uses a Managed Apple Account, stores corporate data separately from personal data, and gives IT a limited set of management capabilities that doesn't include a full device wipe. Automated device enrollment and Apple Configurator are for organization-owned devices. Device enrollment with Company Portal gives full device management, which the privacy requirement rules out.

prompt: The Apple MDM push certificate used by Intune is due to expire next week. Thousands of iOS and macOS devices are enrolled. What must the administrator do to keep those devices manageable without re-enrolling them?

options.text: Renew the existing push certificate with the same Apple Account that created it
Create a new push certificate with any Apple Account and upload it to Intune
Renew the automated device enrollment token in Apple Business Manager
Re-issue the Apple Volume Purchase Program location token

explanation: The Apple MDM push certificate must be renewed every year with the same Apple Account that originally created it. Otherwise the enrolled devices lose contact and must re-enroll. A new certificate from a different account breaks that link. The automated device enrollment token and the volume purchase location token are separate items that don't keep MDM push communication working.

prompt: A company buys corporate iPads through a reseller linked to its Apple Business Manager account. The iPads must enroll in Intune during Setup Assistant, be supervised, and stop users from removing the management profile. Which approach should the administrator use?

options.text: Device enrollment with the Company Portal app and a device restrictions profile
Account-driven User Enrollment with Managed Apple Accounts
Automated device enrollment using an Apple Business Manager token and an enrollment profile
Web-based device enrollment initiated by each user

explanation: Automated device enrollment links Intune to Apple Business Manager with an enrollment program token, and an enrollment profile then supervises devices during Setup Assistant and can lock the MDM profile against removal. Company Portal device enrollment and web-based enrollment are started by users and don't supervise devices or lock the profile. User Enrollment is intended for personal devices.

prompt: A company issues corporate Android phones that each belong to a single employee. Employees may install personal apps, and the company wants personal apps and data kept separate from corporate data, with the company still managing the whole device. Which Android Enterprise enrollment profile should the administrator use?

options.text: Corporate-owned, fully managed user devices
Corporate-owned devices with a work profile
Corporate-owned dedicated devices
Personally owned devices with a work profile

explanation: The corporate-owned work profile scenario (COPE) gives the organization device-level management and keeps a separate work profile for corporate apps and data next to the user's personal space. Fully managed devices have no separate personal space. Dedicated devices are locked down for a specific task and not tied to one user. The personally owned work profile is for BYOD, where the organization can't manage the whole device.

prompt: A warehouse has Android scanners shared by workers across shifts. Each worker signs in to supported apps at the start of a shift and signs out at the end, and data from the previous user must not be left in those apps. Which enrollment option should the administrator choose?

options.text: A fully managed enrollment profile with the default corporate token
A personally owned work profile with Company Portal sign-in
A corporate-owned work profile enrollment profile with a staging token
A dedicated enrollment profile using the Entra shared device mode token

explanation: Android Enterprise dedicated devices enrolled with the Microsoft Entra shared device mode token type let workers sign in and out of apps that support shared device mode, and their data is cleared when they sign out. Fully managed and corporate-owned work profile enrollments are meant for devices assigned to a single user. A personally owned work profile is for BYOD.

prompt: A reseller registers a company's new Samsung Galaxy phones only in Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment. The phones must enroll as Android Enterprise fully managed devices automatically on first boot, with no QR code or token typed by the user. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a Google zero-touch configuration that points to the Intune agent
Give users the QR code from a fully managed enrollment profile
Create a Knox MDM profile that passes the Intune enrollment token in custom JSON
Enroll the phones with Android device administrator and Company Portal

explanation: With Knox Mobile Enrollment, the administrator creates an Android Enterprise MDM profile in the Knox Admin Portal that points to the Intune agent and includes the Intune enrollment token in the custom JSON data, so the devices enroll automatically when first powered on. Zero-touch only works for devices the reseller registered in Google's zero-touch portal, which didn't happen here. A QR code requires user action at setup. Device administrator is a legacy mode, not fully managed Android Enterprise.

prompt: A team of support technicians needs to view devices and users in Intune and run remote tasks such as restart and sync. They must not be able to create or edit policies or apps. Which built-in Intune role should the administrator assign?

options.text: Help Desk Operator
Policy and Profile Manager
Read Only Operator
Windows 365 Administrator

explanation: The Help Desk Operator built-in role runs remote tasks on users and devices and can assign existing apps or policies, but it can't create or edit them. Policy and Profile Manager allows managing compliance and configuration policies, which is too much access. Read Only Operator can't run remote tasks. Windows 365 Administrator is a Microsoft Entra role for managing Cloud PCs, not general Intune help desk work.

prompt: A global company has separate IT teams for Europe and North America. Each team must see and manage only its own region's devices and configuration profiles in the Intune admin center. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Assignment filters that include only each region's devices in every policy
Microsoft Entra administrative units containing each region's users
Scope tags on each region's objects and on the matching role assignments
Scope groups in each role assignment, without any scope tags

explanation: Scope tags limit which Intune objects (devices, policies, apps) an administrator can see, when the tags are applied to the objects and included in the administrator's role assignment. Assignment filters change which devices a policy applies to, not what administrators can see. Administrative units scope Microsoft Entra administration, not Intune objects. Scope groups set which groups an administrator can manage but don't hide other objects in the console.

prompt: To protect against a compromised administrator account, the security team requires that any wipe, retire, or delete action on devices be approved by a second administrator. What should the Intune administrator create?

options.text: A Multi Admin Approval access policy with the Device actions profile type and an approver group
A custom Intune role that removes the wipe permission from all administrators
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for the Intune admin center
A Privileged Identity Management assignment for the Intune Administrator role

explanation: Multi Admin Approval access policies for Device actions protect wipe, retire and delete actions. The action isn't applied until a member of the approver group approves it, and the requester then completes it. Removing the permission prevents the action entirely instead of requiring approval. MFA and PIM make sign-in and role activation harder, but they don't require a second administrator to approve each action.

prompt: An organization uses a Conditional Access policy that requires compliant devices. Auditors found that enrolled devices with no compliance policy assigned are still reported as compliant. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Lower the 'Compliance status validity period' to one day
Add a 'Mark device noncompliant' action to every existing compliance policy
Change the device platform restriction so that only corporate devices can enroll
Set 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' to Not compliant

explanation: The tenant-wide compliance policy setting 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' is Compliant by default. Setting it to Not compliant makes devices without a policy fail compliance. The validity period controls how long a device can go without reporting before it's noncompliant. Changing actions on existing policies doesn't affect devices that have no policy. Enrollment restrictions don't change compliance evaluation.

prompt: Only devices that are enrolled in Intune and meet the company's compliance policies may access Exchange Online and SharePoint Online. The administrator wants to see the policy's effect on users before it starts blocking access. What should the administrator do?

options.text: A device configuration profile that blocks Outlook on noncompliant devices
A Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device, started in Report-only mode
An app protection policy targeted at Exchange Online and SharePoint Online
A noncompliance action that retires noncompliant devices immediately

explanation: A Conditional Access policy with the 'Require device to be marked as compliant' grant uses the Intune compliance state to allow or block access. Report-only mode shows its effect before enforcement. Configuration profiles and app protection policies don't control access to cloud apps based on compliance state. Retiring devices immediately removes management instead of controlling access, and it would be disruptive.

prompt: An organization wants to pilot Windows Hello for Business on a small group of Windows devices before rolling it out to everyone. The tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business enrollment setting currently applies to all users. How should the administrator configure the pilot?

options.text: Set the tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business enrollment setting to Enabled
A compliance policy for the pilot group that requires a six-digit device PIN
A Windows app protection policy that requires a PIN for the pilot group
Set the tenant-wide setting to Not configured and assign a WHfB policy to the pilot group

explanation: The Windows Hello for Business setting under enrollment applies to the whole tenant. To target a pilot, set it to Not configured and assign an endpoint security account protection policy or a settings catalog profile to the pilot group. Enabling the tenant-wide setting affects every user. A compliance policy or an app protection PIN doesn't provision Windows Hello for Business credentials.

prompt: An administrator assigned a Windows LAPS account protection policy that backs up the local administrator password to Microsoft Entra ID for Microsoft Entra joined devices. The policy reports success, but no passwords appear for the devices. What is the most likely missing step?

options.text: Installing the legacy Microsoft LAPS client on each device
Turning on the LAPS setting in Microsoft Entra device settings
Assigning the Endpoint Security Manager role to each primary user
Changing the backup directory to on-premises Active Directory

explanation: Backing up passwords to Microsoft Entra ID from Microsoft Entra joined devices requires the 'Enable Microsoft Entra Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS)' device setting to be turned on. Windows LAPS is built into supported Windows versions, and the Intune CSP-based policy takes precedence over legacy LAPS, so the legacy client isn't needed. Roles for end users don't affect backup. On-premises Active Directory backup can't work for devices that aren't domain joined.

prompt: On a set of engineering Windows devices, the local Administrators group must contain only a specific Microsoft Entra group and the built-in Administrator account. Any other members must be removed. What should the administrator deploy?

options.text: An account protection Local user group membership policy using the Add (Replace) action
Assign the Microsoft Entra Joined Device Local Administrator role to the engineering group
A Windows LAPS policy that manages the built-in Administrator account
A compliance policy that requires the device to have no local administrators

explanation: The Local user group membership policy with the Add (Replace) action replaces the local group's membership with the members you specify, and it can be assigned to only the engineering devices. The Entra Joined Device Local Administrator role applies to every Entra joined device and doesn't remove other members. LAPS manages the password of one account but not group membership. A compliance policy only reports status and doesn't change group membership.

prompt: A company wants to modernise Windows provisioning, but its new laptops must be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined because line-of-business apps still depend on on-premises Active Directory computer accounts. Which Windows Autopilot option should the administrator use for these laptops?

options.text: A Windows Autopilot device preparation policy in user-driven mode
A Windows Autopilot device preparation policy in automatic mode
An Autopilot deployment profile for hybrid join, plus a Domain Join profile
Windows Autopilot Reset run against each of the new laptops

explanation: Windows Autopilot deployment profiles support Microsoft Entra hybrid join, together with a Domain Join device configuration profile and the Intune Connector for Active Directory. Windows Autopilot device preparation, in either user-driven or automatic mode, supports only Microsoft Entra join. Autopilot Reset returns an existing device to a business-ready state and doesn't provision new hybrid-joined devices.

prompt: A retailer is deploying Windows devices as lobby kiosks with no assigned user. The devices should provision themselves after they're connected to a wired network and powered on, with nobody entering credentials. Which Windows Autopilot deployment mode should be used?

options.text: User-driven mode
Self-deploying mode
Pre-provisioning followed by user-driven setup
Existing devices deployment with a JSON file

explanation: Self-deploying mode provisions a device with no user interaction and no user affinity. It uses the device's TPM 2.0 to authenticate and supports Microsoft Entra join, which fits shared kiosks. User-driven mode needs a user to sign in. Pre-provisioning still finishes with a user phase. The existing devices JSON method is for re-provisioning devices that already run Windows, not for unattended kiosk setup.

prompt: Users at a branch with slow internet connections complain that Autopilot setup takes hours because large apps download during the user phase. The company has a staging centre where IT technicians can prepare devices before shipping them. Which approach should the administrator use?

options.text: Self-deploying mode so that users never sign in
Turn off the Enrollment Status Page so that users reach the desktop sooner
Deliver the apps later with Windows Autopilot Reset
Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning, with technicians starting the technician flow on each device

explanation: With pre-provisioning, a technician starts the technician flow during OOBE (by pressing the Windows key five times) so that device-targeted apps and policies install before the device ships. The user's later setup then has much less to download. Self-deploying mode removes the user but doesn't fit user-assigned laptops. Turning off the ESP lets users reach a device that isn't configured yet. Autopilot Reset is a recovery action, not a staging method.

prompt: Microsoft Entra joined devices deployed through a Windows Autopilot deployment profile must be named with the prefix NY- followed by random characters. Which device name template should the administrator enter?

options.text: NY-%USERNAME%
NY-%RAND:15%
NY-%RAND:6%
NY_%COMPUTERNAME%

explanation: Autopilot device name templates support the %SERIAL% and %RAND:x% macros, and the resulting name can't be longer than 15 characters. NY-%RAND:6% gives a 9-character name. %USERNAME% and %COMPUTERNAME% aren't supported Autopilot naming macros. NY-%RAND:15% would produce an 18-character name, which is over the 15-character limit.

prompt: During Autopilot, users reach the desktop before a required security agent finishes installing and start working on an unprotected device. Other required apps can finish in the background. How should the administrator configure the Enrollment Status Page?

options.text: Set 'Block device use until required apps are installed' to Yes and select only the security agent as a blocking app
Set 'Show app and profile configuration progress' to No
Set 'Allow users to reset device if installation error occurs' to Yes
Lower 'Show an error when installation takes longer than specified number of minutes' to 10

explanation: When the Enrollment Status Page blocks device use until the selected required apps are installed, users can't reach the desktop before the security agent is installed. Choosing only that app keeps setup time short. Hiding progress turns off the tracking that enforces the block. Allowing a reset only changes what happens after an error. A shorter timeout makes setup fail sooner and doesn't make the agent install first.

prompt: Before upgrading the Windows 10 fleet to Windows 11, the administrator wants a report in Intune that shows which devices meet the Windows 11 hardware requirements and lists known app or driver compatibility risks. Which prerequisite must be in place for that report to have data?

options.text: Deploy a Windows 11 feature update policy to every device
Register every device with the Windows Autopatch service
Turn on the Windows data connector for Windows diagnostic data
Assign an Endpoint Privilege Management elevation settings policy

explanation: The Windows feature update readiness and compatibility reports rely on Windows diagnostic data. The tenant must turn on the Windows data setting under Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens and confirm Windows licensing. Deploying a feature update policy would start upgrades rather than assess readiness first. Autopatch enrollment isn't the prerequisite for diagnostic data. EPM has nothing to do with upgrade readiness.

prompt: Cloud PCs for a finance team must be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined so that they can use existing on-premises Group Policy. When the administrator creates the Windows 365 Enterprise provisioning policy, what must be selected?

options.text: Hybrid Microsoft Entra join with an Azure network connection
Microsoft Entra join with the Microsoft hosted network
Hybrid Microsoft Entra join with the Microsoft hosted network
Microsoft Entra join with a custom image containing domain settings

explanation: A Windows 365 provisioning policy that uses Hybrid Microsoft Entra join requires an Azure network connection (ANC) to a virtual network with line of sight to Active Directory. The Microsoft hosted network is only available with Microsoft Entra join. A custom image can't replace the hybrid join type and network connection that the policy defines.

prompt: When users get replacement Windows 11 laptops, they want their Windows settings and pinned apps from the old device restored during setup. The new laptops are Microsoft Entra joined through user-driven Autopilot. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Enable Enterprise State Roaming and OneDrive Known Folder Move
Run the User State Migration Tool as a Win32 app during the ESP
Use Autopilot self-deploying mode together with a restore script
Enable Windows backup by policy and turn on the backup and restore enrollment setting

explanation: Windows Backup for organizations needs backup turned on for devices (the 'Enable Windows backup' settings catalog setting). Restore is turned on with the tenant-wide Windows backup and restore enrollment setting, which offers a restore page during OOBE on Microsoft Entra joined devices. Enterprise State Roaming and Known Folder Move don't provide this backup and restore experience. USMT is an on-premises migration tool that isn't integrated into setup this way. Restore isn't supported with self-deploying mode.

prompt: A small software vendor gives the company an ADMX file and its matching ADML language file for a line-of-business app. The settings aren't in the settings catalog. The administrator wants to configure them from the Intune UI rather than by writing OMA-URI strings. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Import the vendor's GPO backup into Group Policy analytics and migrate it
Import the ADMX and ADML files, then use an Imported Administrative templates profile
Create a custom profile and paste the ADMX content into one OMA-URI setting
Upload the ADML file to the settings catalog as a custom definition

explanation: Intune can import custom or third-party ADMX files together with their ADML language files. The settings then appear in an Imported Administrative templates profile that you configure in the UI. Group Policy analytics analyses exported GPO reports, not vendor ADMX files. Ingesting ADMX through a custom OMA-URI is the manual method the administrator wants to avoid. The settings catalog doesn't accept uploaded ADML files.

prompt: An organization moving from Group Policy to Intune wants to find out which settings in its existing GPOs have an equivalent MDM setting, and then move the supported settings into Intune with as little manual work as possible. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Import each GPO's ADMX files and rebuild every setting manually
Deploy a security baseline and remove settings that conflict with GPOs
Create a custom OMA-URI profile for each registry value in the GPOs
Import GPO XML reports into Group Policy analytics and migrate them

explanation: Group Policy analytics imports GPO XML reports, shows which settings have MDM support, and can migrate the supported settings into a settings catalog policy. Rebuilding settings from ADMX files or writing OMA-URI entries takes much more manual work. A security baseline applies Microsoft's recommended settings and doesn't analyse the organization's own GPOs.

prompt: An administrator must configure a Windows CSP setting that is documented in the Policy CSP but isn't yet available in the settings catalog or any template. Which profile type should be used?

options.text: An Imported Administrative templates profile
A Custom profile with an OMA-URI setting
A Device restrictions template profile
A Group Policy analytics migration

explanation: A Windows Custom profile lets you enter the OMA-URI, data type and value for any CSP setting the device supports, including settings not yet exposed in the UI. Imported Administrative templates only contain settings from ADMX files you've imported. The Device restrictions template only offers predefined settings. Group Policy analytics migrates GPO settings and doesn't author arbitrary CSP values.

prompt: Corporate Android phones from several manufacturers are enrolled as Android Enterprise fully managed devices. Security requires blocking screen capture and factory reset from Settings across the whole device. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A device restrictions profile for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices
An app protection policy that blocks screen capture in managed apps
A device restrictions profile for personally owned work profile devices
An OEMConfig profile created separately for each manufacturer

explanation: The Android Enterprise device restrictions profile for fully managed, dedicated, and corporate-owned work profile devices includes device-wide controls such as blocking screen capture and factory reset. App protection policies only protect data inside managed apps. Personally owned work profile restrictions can't control the whole device. OEMConfig is vendor-specific and would mean separate configuration for each manufacturer when a standard setting already covers the requirement.

prompt: An iOS device restrictions profile is assigned to all company iPhones. The settings apply on phones enrolled through automated device enrollment, but several settings are ignored on phones that users enrolled themselves through the Company Portal. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The Apple MDM push certificate expired for those devices
The profile needs an assignment filter for corporate ownership
Those settings need supervision, which Company Portal enrollment doesn't provide
iOS device restrictions apply only to User Enrollment devices

explanation: Many iOS restrictions apply only to supervised devices. Automated device enrollment supervises devices, but user-initiated device enrollment through the Company Portal doesn't. An expired push certificate would stop management of all devices, not just some settings. A filter decides which devices get the profile and doesn't cause individual settings to be ignored. User Enrollment actually supports fewer restrictions, not more.

prompt: A security agent on managed Macs needs Full Disk Access. Users shouldn't be prompted to approve it in System Settings. Which configuration should the administrator deploy?

options.text: A system extensions policy that allows the agent's team ID
A PPPC policy that grants the agent Full Disk Access
A FileVault policy that escrows the recovery key to Intune
A Gatekeeper setting that allows identified developers

explanation: Privacy Preferences Policy Control payloads, available in the settings catalog, can pre-approve privacy permissions such as Full Disk Access for a specific app so users aren't prompted. System extension policies allow an extension to load but don't grant privacy access. FileVault encrypts the disk. Gatekeeper controls which apps may run, not their privacy permissions.

prompt: An organization has Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows systems and Teams panels running Android. The administrator wants to manage device settings beyond the shipped defaults. Which approach is correct?

options.text: Android Enterprise configuration profiles in Intune for both device types
Windows configuration profiles in Intune for both device types
Group Policy objects linked to the room accounts for both device types
Intune Windows profiles for Teams Rooms on Windows; Teams admin center for Android devices

explanation: Teams Rooms on Windows are Windows devices, so Intune can apply Windows configuration profiles and compliance policies to them. Intune doesn't support configuration profiles for Teams Android-based devices such as panels and displays, which are configured with configuration profiles in the Teams admin center. Android profiles don't apply to the Windows systems, and Group Policy can't manage the Android devices.

prompt: Zebra scanners are enrolled as Android Enterprise dedicated devices. The administrator must configure Zebra-specific features such as scanner and battery settings that aren't in the standard Android device restrictions profile. What should the administrator use?

options.text: A Zebra Mobility Extensions (MX) profile uploaded as an XML file
A Wi-Fi profile with custom settings
An app configuration policy for the Zebra OEMConfig app from managed Google Play
A compliance policy with custom settings

explanation: For Android Enterprise devices, OEM-specific features are configured through OEMConfig: you add the Zebra OEMConfig app from managed Google Play and create an OEMConfig profile for it. Zebra MX profiles are for devices enrolled with Android device administrator, not Android Enterprise. Wi-Fi profiles configure only network settings, and compliance policies evaluate settings without configuring them.

prompt: An administrator plans to deploy a Windows edition upgrade profile to new HoloLens 2 devices before applying device restriction settings, because they believe the devices need Windows Holographic for Business first. What should the administrator know?

options.text: No edition upgrade is needed; HoloLens 2 already runs Holographic for Business
HoloLens 2 must first be upgraded to Windows 11 Enterprise
HoloLens 2 can be managed only with Android Enterprise profiles
HoloLens 2 must be enrolled with Apple automated device enrollment

explanation: HoloLens 2 devices run Windows Holographic for Business by default and can be managed with Intune configuration profiles straight away. An edition upgrade was only needed for first-generation HoloLens devices running the base Holographic edition. HoloLens doesn't run Windows 11 Enterprise, and Android and Apple enrollment methods don't apply to it.

prompt: A Windows configuration profile is assigned to the All devices virtual group, but it must apply only to Surface laptops. The administrator doesn't want to create or maintain more groups. What should the administrator configure on the assignment?

options.text: A scope tag named Surface
An excluded group that contains non-Surface devices
An assignment filter on the model property in Include mode
A dynamic device group based on the model

explanation: Assignment filters evaluate device properties such as model and manufacturer when the policy is applied, so a filter in Include mode narrows the All devices assignment without extra groups. Scope tags control what administrators can see, not where policies apply. An exclusion group and a dynamic group would both mean creating and maintaining more groups.

prompt: Standard users must be able to run a specific vendor installer with administrator rights. Each time, they must confirm the elevation and enter a business justification, without waiting for IT to approve it. Endpoint Privilege Management is licensed and the EPM client is deployed. Which elevation rule type should the administrator configure?

options.text: User confirmed, requiring a business justification
Automatic, scoped to the installer's file hash
Support approved, with requests sent to IT
Deny, with a custom message shown to users

explanation: User confirmed rules let users choose 'Run with elevated access' and can require a business justification, Windows authentication, or both, with no approval from IT. Automatic rules elevate silently with no justification. Support approved rules need an administrator to approve each request. Deny rules block the file from running elevated.

prompt: An installer elevated through an EPM rule fails because it needs the signed-in user's profile paths and environment variables. The rule currently uses a type that elevates through an EPM virtual account. Which change resolves the problem while still using EPM?

options.text: Add the user to the local Administrators group
Change the default elevation response to Deny all requests
Turn off child process control on the rule
Change the rule's elevation type to Elevate as current user

explanation: Elevate as current user runs the elevated process under the signed-in user's own account, so it keeps access to user-specific resources such as profile paths and environment variables. It should be scoped tightly because it gives less isolation than a virtual account. Adding users to local Administrators defeats the purpose of EPM. Denying all requests and changing child process behaviour don't give the installer access to the user's profile.

prompt: An organization assigns an Enterprise App Catalog app as Required to all Windows devices. It wants new versions published in the catalog to reach devices automatically, without creating a new app and a supersedence relationship for each release. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Change the assignment to Available for enrolled devices
Turn on auto-update for the Enterprise App Catalog app's required assignment
Repackage the app as a Win32 app with IntuneWinAppUtil
Deploy the app as a Microsoft Store app

explanation: Auto-update for Enterprise App Catalog apps with a Required assignment detects new catalog versions and updates targeted devices without new apps or supersedence. Available assignments keep using the guided supersedence workflow, so switching to Available would lose automatic updates. Repackaging the app yourself, or moving it to the Store, gives up the Microsoft-maintained catalog package rather than meeting the requirement.

prompt: An administrator deploys a non-self-updating Enterprise App Catalog app as Available to users. A newer version now appears in the catalog. How does Intune help the administrator move users to the new version?

options.text: Intune installs the new version automatically on all devices overnight
Download and package the new version yourself as a LOB app
Uninstall the old version with a remediation script, then re-add it
Use the 'apps with updates' view and guided supersedence to add the new version

explanation: For apps without auto-update, such as apps assigned as Available, Intune lists available versions in 'Enterprise App Catalog apps with updates', and guided supersedence creates the new catalog app that supersedes the earlier one. Automatic installation only happens with auto-update on Required assignments. Repackaging as LOB or uninstalling with scripts isn't needed, because the catalog supplies the prepared Win32 package.

prompt: Tier 1 support staff should only be able to view a user's screen during Remote Help sessions. Tier 2 staff should be able to take full control and respond to UAC elevation prompts. Remote Help is turned on for the tenant. How should the administrator meet this requirement?

options.text: The Help Desk Operator role for both tiers, letting users pick the session type
Custom roles with different Remote Help app permissions for each tier
Allow Remote Help on unenrolled devices for Tier 1 only
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for Tier 2 only

explanation: Remote Help uses Intune role-based access control: the Remote Help app permissions in custom roles control whether a helper can view the screen, take full control or use elevation. Help Desk Operator alone doesn't separate the two tiers. The unenrolled-devices setting controls which devices can be helped, not what each helper can do. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions, not session capabilities.

prompt: Field technicians want to use Remote Help to connect to Android ruggedised devices mounted in delivery vans, without a driver accepting each session. What must be true for this unattended connection?

options.text: The devices must be enrolled in Intune as Android Enterprise dedicated devices
The devices must be personally owned devices with a work profile
The devices only need the Remote Help web app
The devices must be unenrolled and use app protection policies

explanation: Remote Help unattended control on Android requires devices to be enrolled in Intune as Android Enterprise dedicated devices. Personally owned work profile devices don't support unattended control. The web app is a view-only option for sharers on desktop platforms. Unenrolled devices with only app protection policies can't be controlled remotely this way.

prompt: A company wants to issue Wi-Fi authentication certificates to Intune-managed Windows, iOS and Android devices without running an on-premises certification authority, NDES, or the Intune Certificate Connector. After it creates a Microsoft Cloud PKI root CA and issuing CA, which two profile types must it deploy to the devices? (Choose two.)

options.text: PKCS certificate profile
Trusted certificate profiles for the root and issuing CA certificates
PKCS imported certificate profile
SCEP certificate profile that uses the issuing CA's SCEP URI
Derived credential profile

explanation: Cloud PKI requires trusted certificate profiles so devices trust the root and issuing CAs, plus a platform-specific SCEP certificate profile that points to the Cloud PKI registration authority's SCEP URI to request leaf certificates. PKCS and PKCS imported profiles rely on the Intune Certificate Connector, which the company wants to avoid. Derived credentials are for smart card scenarios on mobile devices.

prompt: An organization already has an Active Directory Certificate Services root CA that its relying parties trust. It wants Microsoft Cloud PKI to issue certificates to Intune devices while keeping that existing root. What should the administrator create in Cloud PKI?

options.text: A new Cloud PKI root CA and a Cloud PKI issuing CA chained to it
A PKCS certificate profile that points to the AD CS root
A Bring your own CA (BYOCA) issuing CA anchored to the existing private root CA
A trusted certificate profile only

explanation: Bring your own CA creates a Cloud PKI issuing CA anchored to an existing private CA, such as AD CS, so certificates chain to the root that relying parties already trust. A new Cloud PKI root would introduce a separate trust chain. PKCS profiles use the on-premises connector rather than Cloud PKI. A trusted certificate profile only distributes trust and doesn't issue certificates.

prompt: Employees use personal Android phones that aren't enrolled in Intune. They need to reach on-premises intranet sites in Microsoft Edge through Microsoft Tunnel, and the organization already runs a Microsoft Tunnel Gateway. With Tunnel for MAM on Android, which app provides the VPN connection on the device?

options.text: The Company Portal app, signed in by the user
The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint app
The Microsoft Authenticator app
Microsoft Edge's built-in VPN

explanation: On Android, Tunnel for MAM provides the VPN through the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint app, and the Company Portal app must also be installed (users don't need to sign in to it). On iOS, the Tunnel for MAM SDK provides the connection instead. Authenticator handles authentication, not the tunnel. Edge doesn't have its own Tunnel VPN client.

prompt: After a configuration change was rolled out, help desk tickets suggest some Windows devices are crashing more often, but nobody knows which devices, models or apps are involved. The tenant has Intune Advanced Analytics. Which capability should the administrator use first to find the regression and the devices that share it?

options.text: A Windows quality updates report
The Enrollment Status Page report
Group Policy analytics
The Anomalies report in endpoint analytics

explanation: The Advanced Analytics Anomalies report tracks device health for regressions in user experience, such as rising crashes after configuration changes, and groups the affected devices. Quality update reports show update status, not crash regressions. The ESP report covers provisioning. Group Policy analytics evaluates GPO migration, not device health.

prompt: An employee is leaving the company. Their personal Android phone is enrolled in Intune with a work profile. The company must remove corporate apps, data and management, and must not touch the employee's personal photos and apps. Which device action should the administrator use?

options.text: Wipe
Delete
Retire
Remote lock

explanation: Retire removes managed apps, corporate data and the management profile but leaves personal data on the device, which is the right choice for BYOD. Wipe restores the device to factory settings and removes personal data. Delete only removes the device record from Intune and doesn't clean the device. Remote lock just locks the screen.

prompt: A Microsoft Entra joined, Intune-managed Windows 11 laptop is being reassigned to a new employee. IT wants to remove the previous user's files, apps and settings but keep the device joined and enrolled so it returns to a business-ready state quickly, without reimaging. Which remote action fits best?

options.text: Autopilot Reset
Retire
Wipe with 'Wipe device, but keep enrollment state and associated user account' selected
Restart

explanation: Autopilot Reset removes personal files, apps and settings while keeping the device's Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment, then reapplies the original settings so it's ready for the next user. Retire removes management. Wipe with the keep-user option preserves the previous user's account association, which defeats the reassignment. Restart doesn't remove any data.

prompt: An administrator has just assigned a new compliance policy and wants one executive's Windows device to check in and evaluate it now, rather than at its next scheduled check-in. Which device action should be used?

options.text: Restart
Collect diagnostics
Sync
Fresh Start

explanation: The Sync action tells the device to check in with Intune immediately and receive newly assigned policies. Restart reboots the device but doesn't directly start a policy check-in. Collect diagnostics uploads logs. Fresh Start reinstalls Windows and removes apps, which is far more disruptive than needed.

prompt: After a configuration rollout, 60 specific Windows devices across several departments need to be restarted. The administrator wants to do this in one operation from the Intune admin center without scripting. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Bulk device actions with the Restart action
A remediation script assigned with a daily schedule
The Restart action on each device's overview page
A Windows update ring with an engaged restart deadline

explanation: Bulk device actions let you choose an action such as Restart and apply it to many selected devices at once from the admin center. Restarting each device individually is the manual approach being avoided. A remediation script would need custom code and runs on a schedule rather than immediately. Update ring deadlines only control restarts for update installation.

prompt: Microsoft releases a security intelligence update for a fast-spreading threat. The security team wants Microsoft Defender Antivirus on selected Windows devices to download the latest definitions now. Which remote action should the administrator run?

options.text: Quick scan with Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Full scan with Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Sync the device with Intune
Update Windows Defender security intelligence

explanation: The 'Update Windows Defender security intelligence' device action makes Defender Antivirus download the latest security intelligence immediately, and it can also be run as a bulk action. Quick and full scans use whatever definitions the device already has. Sync refreshes Intune policy but doesn't force a definitions update.

prompt: A help desk technician read a BitLocker recovery key to a user over the phone to unlock a Microsoft Entra joined device. Policy requires that a key, once disclosed, can't be used again. The disk encryption policy already enables client-driven recovery password rotation. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Run Fresh Start on the device
Run the BitLocker key rotation device action on the device
Delete the recovery key from Microsoft Entra ID
Disable the device in Microsoft Entra ID

explanation: The BitLocker key rotation device action generates a new recovery password and escrows it to Microsoft Entra ID, so the disclosed key is no longer valid. It needs a supported Windows version and a policy with client-driven recovery password rotation turned on. Fresh Start reinstalls Windows without targeting the key. Deleting the escrowed key leaves the device without a recoverable key. Disabling the device blocks sign-in but doesn't change the key.

prompt: Help desk staff have the built-in Help Desk Operator role. The Windows LAPS policy is in place, but the option to rotate a device's local administrator password is unavailable to them. What should the administrator do?

options.text: The Intune Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID
The Microsoft Entra Joined Device Local Administrator role
A LAPS policy that backs up to on-premises Active Directory
A custom Intune role that includes the Rotate Local Admin Password task

explanation: No Intune built-in role, and not the Intune Administrator Entra role either, includes the Rotate Local Admin Password remote task. It must be granted through a custom Intune role that also includes Managed devices: Read and Organization: Read. Local administrator rights on devices don't grant console actions. The backup directory has nothing to do with this permission.

prompt: During a support call, an administrator needs to see a registry value and the BIOS details of a single Windows device right now, without deploying a script and waiting for it to report back. The tenant has Advanced Analytics. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Collect diagnostics, then review the uploaded logs
Device query on the device, using a KQL query
A remediation script package assigned to the device
The device's hardware inventory, which refreshes every seven days

explanation: Device query sends a real-time KQL query to an online Windows device and returns current data, such as registry values and BIOS information, straight away. It requires Advanced Analytics and the Managed devices: Query permission. Collect diagnostics and remediation scripts both involve waiting for uploads or reports. Standard hardware inventory isn't real time.

prompt: A Windows device is failing to apply several policies, and Microsoft support asks for its MDM diagnostic information, event logs and relevant registry keys. The user isn't technical. How can the administrator collect this information remotely?

options.text: Run Collect diagnostics and download the results from Intune
Ask the user to export logs from the Company Portal app
Run Autopilot Reset so the device regenerates its logs
Start a view-only Remote Help session with the user

explanation: The Collect diagnostics remote action gathers logs, event logs and registry data from a managed Windows device and uploads them to Intune, where they can be downloaded from the device's Device diagnostics view. Asking the user to export logs depends on them. Autopilot Reset erases user data and doesn't collect logs. View-only Remote Help doesn't gather diagnostic files.

prompt: A user reports that a required app never installed and a device of theirs isn't showing in Intune. The help desk wants one view of that user's group memberships, assigned policies and apps, app installation failures and enrollment failures. Where should they look?

options.text: Tenant administration > Tenant status
Reports > Endpoint analytics
Troubleshooting + support > Troubleshoot, selecting the user
Devices > Monitor > Device configuration report

explanation: The Troubleshoot pane in Troubleshooting + support shows user-based details: group membership, assignments, app installation failures, enrollment failures and devices. Tenant status shows service health and connectors. Endpoint analytics covers device performance scores. The device configuration report is a policy-focused view and doesn't give a per-user troubleshooting summary.

prompt: A line-of-business app's data folder is being scanned so heavily that the app slows down. The security team wants a dedicated policy, managed separately from the main antivirus settings, that excludes only that folder from Microsoft Defender Antivirus scanning on Windows devices. Which endpoint security profile should the administrator create?

options.text: Antivirus > Windows Security experience
Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus exclusions
Attack surface reduction > Attack surface reduction rules
Firewall > Windows Firewall rules

explanation: The Microsoft Defender Antivirus exclusions profile, under Antivirus policies, manages file, folder, extension and process exclusions in their own policy. The Windows Security experience profile controls what users see in the Windows Security app and settings such as tamper protection. ASR rules have per-rule exclusions but don't exclude folders from antivirus scanning. Firewall rules control network traffic.

prompt: Users of Microsoft Entra joined devices are sometimes locked out by the BitLocker recovery screen after firmware updates and have to call the help desk. The company wants users to retrieve their own recovery keys. What should the administrator confirm?

options.text: The disk encryption policy uses XTS-AES 256 for the OS drive
Each user is assigned the Cloud Device Administrator role
A BitLocker startup PIN is configured on every device
Keys are escrowed to Entra ID and users aren't restricted from recovering them

explanation: When recovery keys are escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID, users can view keys for devices they own through the Company Portal website or My Account, unless the Entra device setting that restricts users from recovering their own BitLocker keys is turned on. The encryption algorithm doesn't affect key retrieval. Cloud Device Administrator is an over-privileged admin role. A startup PIN adds a pre-boot factor but doesn't help users recover keys.

prompt: After assigning a BitLocker disk encryption policy, the administrator needs to see which Windows devices are encrypted, which aren't, and whether each device's TPM makes it ready for encryption. Which Intune view should be used?

options.text: Endpoint analytics startup performance
Microsoft Entra audit logs
The Encryption report under Devices > Monitor
The Windows feature updates report

explanation: The Encryption report shows each device's encryption status and readiness details, such as TPM version, and helps troubleshoot devices that haven't encrypted. Startup performance measures boot and sign-in times. Entra audit logs record directory changes, not encryption state. The feature updates report tracks Windows upgrades.

prompt: An administrator is building several Windows Firewall rules policies, and the same list of partner IP address ranges appears in many rules. The list changes every quarter, and the administrator wants to update it in one place. What should be used?

options.text: A reusable settings group of remote IP addresses referenced by the firewall rules
A separate firewall rules policy for each IP range
A network boundary in a Windows Information Protection policy
An assignment filter that matches the partner IP ranges

explanation: Reusable settings groups let you define remote IP address lists once and reference them from multiple firewall rules, so one change updates every rule that uses the group. Separate policies for each range would multiply maintenance. Windows Information Protection is retired and doesn't feed firewall rules. Assignment filters choose devices based on device properties, not network addresses.

prompt: As part of a Zero Trust initiative, the security team wants to stop Office apps from creating child processes on Windows devices. It's worried about breaking business macros, so it first wants to see which devices would be affected without blocking anything. How should the administrator configure the attack surface reduction rule?

options.text: Set the rule to Block mode for a pilot group only
Turn on network protection in block mode instead
Set the rule to Audit mode and review the reported events
Turn off the rule and rely on App Control for Business

explanation: Audit mode records what an ASR rule would have blocked without enforcing it, so you can judge the impact before switching to Block or Warn. Block mode, even for a pilot group, would disrupt the pilot users' macros. Network protection controls connections to dangerous domains, not Office child processes. App Control for Business restricts which apps can run and doesn't replace this behavioural rule.

prompt: A newer version of the security baseline for Windows is released. The administrator's current baseline profile has several customised settings that must be kept. What is the recommended way to move to the new version?

options.text: Change the existing profile's baseline version and choose to keep the existing setting customisations
Delete the existing profile and create a new one from scratch
Create a settings catalog policy that duplicates the new baseline settings
Keep the old baseline version permanently because baselines can't be updated

explanation: Intune lets you change a baseline profile to a newer version and choose whether to keep your existing customisations or discard them, which keeps assignments and preserves intentional deviations. Recreating the profile loses that history and adds work. Duplicating settings in the settings catalog creates conflicts and loses baseline tracking. Baseline profiles can be updated, so staying on an old version isn't required.

prompt: Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint are connected through the service-to-service connection. The administrator now creates an endpoint detection and response policy to onboard Intune-managed Windows devices to Defender for Endpoint. Which onboarding option should be selected so that the onboarding package doesn't need to be downloaded and uploaded manually?

options.text: Onboard from a file uploaded by the administrator
Offboard
Not configured
Auto from connector

explanation: With the Defender for Endpoint connector in place, the EDR policy's 'Auto from connector' option retrieves the onboarding package from the tenant automatically. Uploading a package file works but is the manual approach the administrator wants to avoid. Offboard removes devices from the service. Not configured onboards nothing.

prompt: When Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detects an active threat that raises a device's machine risk level to High, the security team wants that device blocked from corporate cloud apps until the threat is resolved. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An antivirus policy that runs a full scan every day
A compliance policy with a maximum machine risk score, plus Conditional Access
An attack surface reduction rule set to Block mode
An EDR policy that offboards high-risk devices automatically

explanation: Defender for Endpoint shares each device's machine risk score with Intune. A compliance setting that requires the score to be at or under a chosen level marks higher-risk devices noncompliant, and Conditional Access then blocks them. A daily scan and an ASR rule don't change access. Offboarding devices would remove Defender's visibility instead of containing the risk.

prompt: An organization is deploying an App Control for Business policy in enforced mode. Apps that IT deploys through Intune as Win32 apps must keep running without someone adding rules for each app. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Add each Win32 app's hash as an ASR rule exclusion
Keep the App Control policy in audit mode permanently
Add the Win32 apps to a Defender Antivirus exclusions profile
Make the Intune Management Extension a managed installer and trust it

explanation: Setting the Intune Management Extension as a managed installer tags the apps it installs, and the App Control for Business built-in option to trust apps from managed installers allows those apps to run. ASR exclusions and antivirus exclusions don't change App Control decisions. Staying in audit mode permanently means the policy never enforces anything.

prompt: After a vendor driver update caused display problems, the change board requires that every Windows driver and firmware update offered through Windows Update be reviewed and approved before it reaches devices. What should the administrator configure in Intune?

options.text: A Windows update ring that defers quality updates by 30 days
A Windows driver updates policy that uses manual approval
A feature updates policy for the current Windows 11 version
A device configuration profile that blocks Windows Update

explanation: A Windows driver updates policy with manual approval lists the applicable driver and firmware updates and deploys only the ones an administrator approves. Deferring quality updates only delays all updates and provides no per-driver approval. Feature update policies control the Windows version. Blocking Windows Update would also stop security updates.

prompt: A critical Windows security update has been released. The update ring for most devices defers quality updates by 14 days, but the security team wants this specific update installed within two days, without changing the ring's normal deferral. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A Windows quality update policy that expedites installation of that update
A new update ring with zero deferral that replaces the existing ring
A feature updates policy that targets the latest Windows 11 version
A Delivery Optimization profile with a higher bandwidth limit

explanation: A Windows quality update policy can expedite a specific security update to devices below a chosen build, bypassing the update ring's deferral for that update only. Replacing the ring changes the deferral for every future update. A feature update policy changes the Windows version. Delivery Optimization changes how content is downloaded, not when updates are approved.

prompt: Several users in the Pilot update ring report app crashes after this month's quality update. The administrator wants to stop the quality update from installing on more devices in that ring while the issue is investigated, without affecting other rings. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Delete the Pilot update ring
Set the feature update deferral on the Pilot ring to 365 days
Pause quality updates on the Pilot update ring
Remove the devices from Intune management

explanation: Pausing quality updates on an update ring stops new quality updates for that ring for up to 35 days, and the ring can then be resumed or the update uninstalled. Deleting the ring removes its configuration rather than pausing it. Feature update deferral doesn't affect quality updates. Removing management is far more disruptive than needed.

prompt: Windows 11, version 25H2 is now available, but a critical engineering app is only certified on version 24H2. The administrator wants devices to stay on 24H2 and keep getting quality updates until certification is complete. What should be configured?

options.text: An update ring with the feature update deferral set to 0 days
A feature updates policy that specifies Windows 11, version 24H2
A quality update policy that expedites the latest update
Pause feature updates on the update ring indefinitely

explanation: A feature updates policy keeps targeted devices on the Windows version it specifies, and they keep receiving quality updates for that version. A zero-day feature deferral would let devices move to newer versions sooner. Expediting a quality update doesn't control the version. A feature update pause expires after 35 days, so it can't hold devices indefinitely.

prompt: An organization licensed for Microsoft 365 E3 wants to manage Windows quality and feature updates for several departments through a set of sequential deployment rings. It wants the related update policies, Microsoft Entra groups and ring settings managed together as one unit in the Intune admin center. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Separate update rings created by hand for each department
Group Policy objects for Windows Update for Business
A Delivery Optimization configuration profile
A Windows Autopatch group

explanation: A Windows Autopatch group is a logical container that combines Microsoft Entra groups with software update policies, such as update rings and feature update policies, across sequential deployment rings. Hand-built rings work but are managed individually rather than as one unit. Group Policy isn't managed from Intune. Delivery Optimization only affects how content is downloaded.

prompt: A Windows quality update policy has 'When available, apply without restarting the device (Hotpatch)' set to Allow. Eligible Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 devices are licensed and on the current baseline, but some still receive the standard cumulative update and need a restart. In System Information, those devices don't show Virtualization-based security as Running. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a second hotpatch policy for those devices
Pause quality updates on those devices
Turn on virtualization-based security on those devices
Change those devices to Windows 11 Pro

explanation: Virtualization-based security must be running for a device to be offered hotpatch updates. Devices without it are treated as ineligible and receive the latest cumulative update, which needs a restart. Another hotpatch policy won't fix an eligibility requirement. Pausing updates leaves the devices unpatched. Windows 11 Pro isn't one of the eligible editions.

prompt: Company iPhones running iOS 17 or later must install a specific iOS version by a fixed date and time. After that point the update should install and restart the device automatically. How should the administrator configure this in Intune?

options.text: A settings catalog DDM Software Update policy with a target version and date
A compliance policy that sets the minimum OS version required
A device restrictions profile that defers update visibility for 90 days
An app configuration policy that targets the Settings app

explanation: The settings catalog Declarative Device Management Software Update settings let you set a Target OS Version and a Target Date Time. When the deadline passes, the device forces installation and a restart. A compliance policy only marks outdated devices noncompliant. Deferring update visibility delays updates rather than enforcing them. App configuration policies don't control OS updates.

prompt: Corporate Android Enterprise fully managed devices are used by delivery drivers during the day. Android system updates should install only overnight, between 01:00 and 05:00. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A compliance policy with a minimum security patch level
An app protection policy with a minimum OS version condition
A device restrictions profile with System update set to a maintenance window
A Windows update ring assigned to the Android device group

explanation: The Android Enterprise device restrictions profile for corporate-owned devices has a System update setting that supports Automatic, Postponed and Maintenance window (windowed) options. For specific firmware versions on supported OEM devices, FOTA integrations such as Zebra LifeGuard or Samsung E-FOTA can be used instead. A compliance patch-level check only reports noncompliance. App protection conditions don't install updates, and Windows update rings don't apply to Android.
