prompt: A branch office has a slow WAN link, and its devices sit on several subnets behind NAT. The administrator wants Windows devices in the same Active Directory site to share update content with each other, even across those subnets. How should Delivery Optimization be configured?

options.text: Download mode set to Group (2) with the group ID source set to AD site
Download mode set to HTTP only (0)
Download mode set to Bypass (100)
Download mode set to LAN (1) with no group ID

explanation: Group download mode (2) allows peering beyond the local NAT boundary among devices in the same group, and using the AD site as the group ID source puts the branch devices in one peer group. LAN mode (1) only peers behind the same public IP and NAT. HTTP only turns off peering, and Bypass skips Delivery Optimization altogether.

prompt: An administrator deployed a Windows 11 feature update policy and now needs to see, for each device, whether the update is pending, installing, completed or failed, along with any error details. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: The Enrollment Status Page settings
The device's Remediations status
The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center inventory
The Windows feature update report in Intune reports

explanation: The Windows feature update report shows per-device update states and alerts, including errors, for feature update policies. It relies on Windows diagnostic data being turned on for the tenant. ESP settings control provisioning. Remediations status covers script packages. The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center reports on Office, not Windows feature updates.

prompt: An administrator has an installer folder containing setup.exe and supporting files for a desktop app and wants to deploy it as a Win32 app with detection and requirement rules. What must be done before the app can be uploaded to Intune?

options.text: Convert the installer to an MSIX package with the MSIX tool
Package it as an .intunewin file with the Win32 Content Prep Tool
Sign the installer with a trusted code-signing certificate
Compress the folder into a ZIP file and upload the archive

explanation: Win32 apps are uploaded as .intunewin files, which the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool (IntuneWinAppUtil.exe) creates from the source folder and setup file. MSIX conversion isn't required for Win32 deployment. Code signing isn't needed to create a Win32 app. Intune doesn't accept a plain ZIP file as a Win32 app.

prompt: A company wants to deploy a public app from the Microsoft Store as Required to Windows devices, with Intune keeping it up to date. Which app type should the administrator add?

options.text: Microsoft Store for Business app synced to Intune
Windows app (Win32) that wraps the Store installer
Line-of-business app using an .appx file downloaded manually
Microsoft Store app (new)

explanation: The Microsoft Store app (new) type uses the Windows Package Manager integration to deploy and update Store apps, and it can be assigned as Required or Available. The Microsoft Store for Business is retired, so there's nothing to sync. Wrapping the Store installer in a Win32 app or sideloading an .appx adds packaging work and loses Store-managed updates.

prompt: To support wellbeing, the HR department wants Outlook email and Teams notifications on employees' iOS and Android devices muted every weekday after 18:00 and all weekend. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A device restrictions profile that turns on Do Not Disturb
A Quiet Time policy of the Days of the week type under Apps
An app protection policy with a 'Notifications' setting that blocks org data in notifications
An app configuration policy for Outlook that sets a sync schedule

explanation: Quiet Time policies, under Apps > Quiet Time, mute Outlook email and Teams notifications on iOS/iPadOS and Android, using either a Date range or a Days of the week schedule. Device-level Do Not Disturb isn't scheduled per app this way. The app protection notification setting controls whether org data appears in notifications, not when notifications are muted. An Outlook sync schedule isn't a Quiet Time setting.

prompt: An administrator needs to deploy Microsoft 365 Apps to Windows devices, excluding Access and Publisher, using Monthly Enterprise Channel, and removing older MSI versions of Office. The administrator prefers to configure this in the Intune UI without writing XML. What should be used?

options.text: The Microsoft 365 Apps app type with the configuration designer
A line-of-business app that uploads the Office MSI package
A Microsoft Store app (new) added for each Office app
A Group Policy object that runs setup.exe at computer startup

explanation: The built-in Microsoft 365 Apps app type has a configuration designer for choosing apps, the update channel and the option to remove MSI versions, without writing XML. Office isn't deployed as a single MSI line-of-business app. Deploying individual Store apps doesn't give the suite configuration. A GPO startup script isn't an Intune method.

prompt: Office security settings, such as blocking macros from the internet, must apply to users when they sign in to Microsoft 365 Apps on any device, including personal devices that aren't enrolled in Intune. What should the administrator use?

options.text: An Intune settings catalog policy with Office settings assigned to device groups
An Imported Administrative templates profile for Office
A Cloud Policy configuration in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center assigned to a user group
An app protection policy for Windows

explanation: Cloud Policy, managed from the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, applies user-based Office policy settings when the user signs in to Microsoft 365 Apps, whether or not the device is managed. Settings catalog and imported template profiles only reach Intune-enrolled devices. Windows app protection policies protect data in Microsoft Edge, not Office policy settings.

prompt: An administrator has a configuration.xml created with the Office Customization Tool and wants Microsoft 365 Apps installed with that configuration during Windows Autopilot, as a blocking app on the Enrollment Status Page. Which two deployment methods meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: A Microsoft 365 Apps (Windows 10 and later) app that uses the 'Enter XML data' configuration format
A Microsoft Store app (new) for Microsoft 365
A Win32 app that packages the Office Deployment Tool setup.exe with the configuration.xml
A line-of-business app that uploads the configuration.xml file
An iOS store app for Microsoft 365

explanation: The Microsoft 365 Apps app type accepts a custom XML configuration, and a Win32 app can wrap the Office Deployment Tool with configuration.xml (setup.exe /configure). Either can be chosen as a blocking app on the ESP. A Store app doesn't use an ODT configuration. A configuration.xml file isn't a line-of-business app package. iOS store apps don't apply to Windows Autopilot.

prompt: Devices run Microsoft 365 Apps on Monthly Enterprise Channel. The administrator wants Microsoft to handle the monthly update rollout automatically, with the ability to set exclusion dates and roll back problematic builds, and with progress shown in a dashboard. Where should this be configured?

options.text: A Windows quality update policy in Intune
Servicing profiles in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center
A Delivery Optimization profile
A feature updates policy in Intune

explanation: Servicing profiles in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center manage Monthly Enterprise Channel updates for the devices in scope, including exclusion dates, rollback and progress reporting. Windows quality and feature update policies manage Windows, not Microsoft 365 Apps. Delivery Optimization only controls how content is downloaded.

prompt: A school bought 500 licences for a paid iPad app through Apple Business Manager. Students' shared iPads have no Apple Account signed in, and the app must install silently. How should the administrator deploy it?

options.text: Assign the app with user licensing so that each student must sign in with an Apple Account
Upload the app as an iOS line-of-business .ipa file
Add the app as an iOS store app from the public App Store search
Sync the Apps and Books location token in Intune and assign the app as Required with device licensing

explanation: Volume-purchased apps from Apple Business Manager sync into Intune with the Apps and Books location token, and device licensing installs them silently with no Apple Account on the device. User licensing needs users to sign in with an Apple Account. A purchased store app can't be redistributed as an .ipa. An iOS store app added from App Store search isn't tied to the purchased licences, so it can't be installed silently without an Apple Account.

prompt: A Win32 app shows 'Failed' in its device install status for several Windows devices, and the error code doesn't make the cause clear. Which client-side logs should the administrator review on an affected device?

options.text: C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log and the CBS persist logs
The Company Portal app logs collected from an iOS device
C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs
C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\ReportingEvents.log

explanation: The Intune Management Extension installs Win32 apps and writes detailed logs, including detection, download and installation steps, under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs. CBS.log records Windows component servicing. iOS Company Portal logs don't cover Windows apps. ReportingEvents.log relates to Windows Update.

prompt: Employees read corporate email in Outlook on personal iPhones and Android phones that aren't enrolled in Intune. The company must stop users from copying corporate data into personal apps or saving attachments to personal cloud storage, and it can't manage the devices themselves. What should the administrator create?

options.text: An app protection policy that restricts transfer and saving of org data
A device restrictions profile that blocks sharing on iOS and Android
A compliance policy that requires a passcode and encryption
An app configuration policy for managed devices that sets Outlook options

explanation: App protection policies work at the app level without device enrollment. Their data protection settings can restrict transfer to policy-managed apps and block saving copies of org data to unmanaged storage. Device restrictions profiles and managed-device app configuration policies need enrolled devices. A compliance policy evaluates device state and doesn't control data movement between apps.

prompt: The security team requires that corporate data in managed mobile apps can't be accessed on jailbroken iOS or rooted Android devices, and that org data in those apps is removed when such a device is detected. Which app protection policy section should the administrator configure?

options.text: Data protection, with 'Restrict cut, copy, and paste' set to Blocked
Access requirements, with a PIN of six digits
Conditional launch, with the jailbroken/rooted devices condition set to wipe data
Assignments, excluding jailbroken devices with a filter

explanation: Conditional launch settings check conditions such as jailbroken or rooted status when the app starts, and they can block access or wipe org data. Clipboard restrictions limit data movement but don't check device integrity. A PIN requirement doesn't detect jailbreaks. Filters can't reliably target jailbroken status for unmanaged devices, and an exclusion would leave those devices without protection.

prompt: Policy states that if a managed app on an unenrolled phone hasn't checked in with Intune for 90 days, the org data in that app must be removed automatically. Which app protection setting meets this requirement?

options.text: An Offline grace period condition set to wipe data after 90 days
Recheck the access requirements after 90 days of inactivity
A minimum app version condition with the action set to warn
Block backup of org data to iTunes and iCloud backups

explanation: The Offline grace period conditional launch setting can block access after a short time offline and wipe org data after a longer number of days without check-in, such as 90. Rechecking access requirements after inactivity only re-prompts for the PIN or credentials. A minimum app version check is unrelated to check-in time. Blocking backups prevents copies but doesn't remove data.

prompt: Contractors use personal Windows PCs that aren't enrolled in Intune to access corporate web apps. The company wants to protect org data in the browser, for example by blocking copy to personal apps and printing, without managing the PCs. What should the administrator implement?

options.text: A Windows Information Protection policy without enrollment
Windows Autopilot self-deploying mode for the contractor PCs
A Windows compliance policy assigned to the contractor group
An app protection policy for Windows targeting Edge, with Conditional Access

explanation: Intune app protection for Windows targets Microsoft Edge on unmanaged personal devices to control data actions such as copy, paste and print, and Conditional Access requires the protected browser experience. Windows Information Protection is retired. Autopilot would provision corporate devices, not personal ones. Compliance policies need enrollment.

prompt: A user left the company. Their personal phone isn't enrolled in Intune, but the Outlook and OneDrive apps on it are protected by an app protection policy. The company must remove corporate data from those apps without affecting anything else on the phone. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Send a full device wipe
Create an app selective wipe request for the user's device
Retire the device from the Devices list
Delete the user's licence and wait for the data to disappear

explanation: An app selective wipe request removes org data only from the app protection-managed apps on the user's devices, which works without device enrollment. A full device wipe or retire requires an MDM-enrolled device, and a full wipe would also remove personal data. Removing a licence doesn't reliably remove data that's already cached in the apps.

prompt: The organization wants a stricter app protection policy for apps on personal phones that aren't enrolled in Intune, and a lighter policy for the same apps on Intune-enrolled corporate phones. How can the administrator target each policy?

options.text: Use scope tags to separate the strict and lighter policies
Create both policies as device configuration profiles instead
Assign both policies to one group so Intune merges the settings
Target each policy by device management type: unmanaged or managed

explanation: App protection policies can target apps by device management type, such as unmanaged versus managed devices (or use filters for managed apps), so different policies apply depending on whether the device is enrolled. Scope tags control administrator visibility. Device configuration profiles don't provide app-level data protection on unmanaged devices. Assigning conflicting policies to one group doesn't produce the intended split.

prompt: Access to Exchange Online from iOS and Android must be allowed only from apps protected by an Intune app protection policy, whether or not the device is enrolled. Which Conditional Access grant control should the administrator use?

options.text: Require device to be marked as compliant
Require app protection policy
Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Require terms of use

explanation: The 'Require app protection policy' grant only allows access from client apps that have an Intune app protection policy applied, which works on unenrolled devices. A compliant-device requirement needs enrollment. Hybrid join doesn't apply to mobile devices. Terms of use only shows an acceptance screen.

prompt: After a Conditional Access policy requiring app protection is turned on for Exchange Online, users who read mail in the built-in iOS Mail app are blocked, but Outlook users aren't. What explains this?

options.text: The built-in Mail app doesn't support Intune app protection policies
The iOS Mail app requires a separate device compliance policy
The users don't have an Exchange Online licence assigned
The Conditional Access policy is still in report-only mode

explanation: The 'Require app protection policy' grant only allows apps that integrate with Intune app protection, such as Outlook. The native iOS Mail app doesn't, so it's blocked. A compliance policy wouldn't make the Mail app meet an app protection requirement. A licensing problem would also block Outlook. A report-only policy doesn't block anyone.

prompt: The organization wants to allow access to SharePoint Online from mobile devices that are either enrolled and compliant, or unenrolled but using an app with an app protection policy. How should the Conditional Access grant be configured, using the 'Require device to be marked as compliant' and 'Require app protection policy' controls?

options.text: Select both grants with 'Require all the selected controls'
Select only 'Require device to be marked as compliant'
Select both grants with 'Require one of the selected controls'
Block access, with an exclusion for compliant devices

explanation: With 'Require one of the selected controls', either a compliant device or an app protected by an app protection policy satisfies the policy. Requiring all selected controls would force unenrolled devices to be compliant, which they can't be. Requiring only compliance blocks the BYOD scenario. A block-with-exclusion design doesn't allow app protection-only access.

prompt: A Conditional Access policy requires app protection for mobile access to Microsoft 365. Users on unenrolled iPhones and Android phones are prompted to install another app before they can sign in to Outlook. Which apps provide the brokered authentication on each platform?

options.text: Microsoft Edge on both platforms
Microsoft Authenticator on iOS, and Intune Company Portal on Android
Intune Company Portal on iOS, and Microsoft Authenticator on Android
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on both platforms

explanation: For app-based Conditional Access, Microsoft Authenticator acts as the broker on iOS/iPadOS, and the Company Portal app is required on Android, even though users don't enroll the device. Edge is a protected app, not the broker. Swapping the platforms is incorrect. Defender for Endpoint provides threat protection and Tunnel for MAM on Android, not the Conditional Access broker.

prompt: On Intune-enrolled iOS devices, Outlook must allow only the user's corporate account to be added, and the account must be pre-filled. Which configuration should the administrator deploy?

options.text: An app protection policy that requires work or school credentials
A managed apps app configuration policy that sets a home page URL
A device restrictions profile that blocks account modification
Managed devices app configuration with Outlook's allowed-account keys

explanation: On enrolled devices, a managed devices app configuration policy can deliver the IntuneMAMAllowedAccountsOnly and IntuneMAMUPN keys, using the {{userprincipalname}} token, so Outlook allows only the corporate account and pre-fills it. Requiring work credentials in app protection is an access check and doesn't restrict which accounts can be added. A home page URL setting is unrelated. Blocking account modification is a device-wide setting that doesn't pre-fill Outlook.

prompt: Users on unenrolled personal phones use Microsoft Edge for work. The company wants Edge to show corporate managed bookmarks and a corporate home page when users are signed in with their work account. Which policy should the administrator create?

options.text: An app configuration policy for managed devices
A device configuration profile for Edge
An app configuration policy for managed apps targeting Microsoft Edge
A compliance policy for Edge

explanation: App configuration policies for managed apps deliver settings through the Intune App SDK to apps such as Edge, with no device enrollment, and apply in the work account context. Managed devices app configuration and device configuration profiles both need enrolled devices. Compliance policies don't configure app settings.

prompt: A line-of-business Android app from managed Google Play runs on fully managed devices and needs location access. Users must not be prompted to grant the permission. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An app configuration policy for managed devices that sets the location permission to Auto grant
An app protection policy that allows location
A device restrictions profile that turns on location services for all apps
An app configuration policy for managed apps with a location key

explanation: For Android Enterprise, app configuration policies for managed devices include a Permissions section where runtime permissions such as location can be set to Auto grant for a specific app. App protection policies don't grant OS permissions. Turning on location services device-wide doesn't grant the app's runtime permission. Managed apps configuration delivers SDK-based settings, not OS permissions.

prompt: A vendor's iOS app reads a configuration key named DeviceSerial at launch to register the device with the vendor's service. The app is deployed to Intune-enrolled iPhones. How should the administrator supply each device's own serial number?

options.text: A separate app configuration policy created for each device
A custom setting in an app protection policy for the app
A managed devices app configuration policy using {{serialnumber}}
Instructions asking users to type the serial on first launch

explanation: Managed devices app configuration policies for iOS support tokens such as {{serialnumber}}, which Intune replaces with each device's value when it delivers the configuration. A separate policy for each device can't be maintained. App protection policies don't deliver arbitrary configuration keys. Relying on users to type the serial number is error-prone and doesn't meet the automation goal.

prompt: A third-party iOS app doesn't integrate the Intune App SDK but supports the standard managed app configuration mechanism. It is deployed to Intune-enrolled devices. Which policy type can deliver its configuration?

options.text: An app configuration policy for managed devices
An app configuration policy for managed apps
An app protection policy
A Quiet Time policy

explanation: Managed devices app configuration policies deliver settings through the MDM channel, which works for apps that support the platform's managed app configuration, even without the Intune SDK. Managed apps configuration and app protection policies require the Intune App SDK or app wrapping. Quiet Time only mutes notifications in supported Microsoft apps.

prompt: An administrator writes a PowerShell script that runs nightly on a server with no signed-in user and exports the list of Intune managed devices through Microsoft Graph. How should the script authenticate?

options.text: The administrator's account, signing in interactively each night
Graph Explorer, reusing the administrator's session token
An app registration with only the User.Read delegated permission
An app registration with an application permission and a certificate

explanation: Unattended automation uses the client credentials flow: an app registration granted the required application permission, here DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All with admin consent, that authenticates with a certificate or secret. Interactive delegated sign-in and Graph Explorer sessions need a user to be present. User.Read doesn't grant access to Intune device data.

prompt: A script uses Connect-MgGraph and then calls the syncDevice action on Intune managed devices. The call fails with an authorization error. The current scopes include only DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All. Which permission must be added?

options.text: DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All
DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All
DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All
Directory.Read.All

explanation: Remote actions such as syncDevice on managed devices need the DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All permission. The configuration and apps permissions cover policies and apps, not device actions. Directory.Read.All reads directory objects and doesn't authorize Intune remote actions.

prompt: A tenant has a Multi Admin Approval access policy that protects Apps. An automation service principal that publishes apps through Microsoft Graph with app-only authentication now has its create requests held for approval. The security team agrees that this one trusted pipeline can bypass approval. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Switch the pipeline to delegated Global Administrator sign-in
Delete the Apps access policy for the whole tenant
Assign the Intune Administrator role to the service principal
Exclude the pipeline's enterprise app in the Apps access policy

explanation: Multi Admin Approval applies to app-only Graph calls on protected resources. Specific enterprise applications can be excluded per access policy, and changing exclusions also requires a second administrator's approval. Delegated calls are always subject to approval, even from Global Administrators. Deleting the policy removes protection for everyone. Assigning a role doesn't bypass approval.

prompt: An administrator sets up the Vulnerability Remediation Agent in the Intune admin center to get prioritised, Intune-specific remediation guidance for CVEs on Windows devices. Security Copilot capacity is available and Intune Plan 1 is licensed. Which other capability must the tenant have for the agent to get its vulnerability data?

options.text: Intune Advanced Analytics
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Windows Autopatch

explanation: The Vulnerability Remediation Agent analyses CVE data from Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, which comes with Defender for Endpoint P2 or Defender Vulnerability Management Standalone. Advanced Analytics provides endpoint performance insights, not CVE data. Entra ID P2 isn't required for this agent. Windows Autopatch manages updates rather than supplying vulnerability findings.

prompt: After setting up the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, an administrator finds that the Run button is unavailable. The setup created the agent's agentic identity in Microsoft Entra ID. What should the administrator do next?

options.text: Delegate permissions to the agentic user and pass the readiness check
Remove the agent and set it up again as a Global Administrator
Assign the agent identity a Windows Enterprise E5 licence
Create a Multi Admin Approval access policy for the agent

explanation: Agent runs stay disabled until the required permissions, such as Intune read permissions and Defender read access, are delegated to the agentic user and the Run Readiness Check succeeds. Recreating the agent doesn't delegate permissions. A Windows licence doesn't apply to the agent identity. Multi Admin Approval protects changes and has nothing to do with enabling agent runs.

prompt: The Vulnerability Remediation Agent shows a high-priority suggestion with step-by-step guidance to deploy an updated browser version through Intune. The administrator deploys the update. What is the appropriate next step in the agent experience?

options.text: Nothing, because the agent already applied the fix
Remove the agent so the suggestion doesn't reappear
Mark the suggestion as applied in the agent
Pause the agent until a new CVE is published

explanation: The agent's suggestions are guidance. The administrator carries out the remediation in Intune and can mark the suggestion as applied, so there's a record to track as later runs refresh CVE details and device counts. The agent doesn't apply changes by itself. Removing the agent deletes its data. Agent runs can't be paused after they start.

prompt: The organization must check that a proprietary security agent's service is running and that a specific registry value exists on Windows devices, and mark devices noncompliant if not. No built-in compliance setting covers this. Which two items must the administrator provide for custom compliance? (Choose two.)

options.text: A PowerShell discovery script that returns the values as JSON
A remediation script that fixes the setting
A JSON file that defines the rules each returned setting is evaluated against
An ADMX file describing the registry value
An app configuration policy for the agent

explanation: Custom compliance for Windows uses a PowerShell discovery script, added under the compliance scripts node, that outputs the settings as JSON, plus a JSON rules file uploaded in the compliance policy that defines operators, operands and remediation text. A remediation script belongs to Remediations, not compliance evaluation. An ADMX file and an app configuration policy don't take part in custom compliance.

prompt: A Windows custom compliance policy reports errors on devices instead of Compliant or Not compliant. The discovery script writes several lines of plain text, such as 'Service running: True'. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Run the discovery script in 32-bit PowerShell instead
Return one compressed JSON object whose keys match the rules file
Convert the discovery script into a remediation package
Increase the compliance status validity period to 60 days

explanation: Custom compliance evaluates the discovery script's JSON output against the rules file, so the script must return valid JSON (typically compressed with ConvertTo-Json -Compress) whose property names match the SettingName entries. The PowerShell bitness doesn't fix invalid output. Remediation packages are a different feature. The validity period doesn't affect parsing.

prompt: The operations team wants to build custom dashboards and queries that combine Intune audit logs and operational (enrollment) logs, keeping the data longer than the Intune admin center does. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Export each Intune report to a CSV file once a month
Assign the Read Only Operator role to the operations team
Configure endpoint analytics baselines for each department
Diagnostic settings that stream the logs to a Log Analytics workspace

explanation: Intune diagnostic settings can stream audit logs, operational logs and other categories to a Log Analytics workspace, where retention is configurable and workbooks and KQL queries can be built. Monthly CSV exports are manual and don't support live dashboards. A role assignment only grants access. Endpoint analytics baselines compare performance scores.

prompt: A business analyst wants to build Power BI reports on historical Intune data, such as device inventory trends and compliance over time, with a scheduled refresh. Which data source should the analyst connect to?

options.text: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center inventory
The Windows Update for Business deployment service
The Intune Data Warehouse OData feed
The Intune Company Portal website

explanation: The Intune Data Warehouse exposes historical Intune data through an OData feed that Power BI can connect to and refresh on a schedule. The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center inventory covers Office installations only. The Windows Update deployment service manages update deployments, not general reporting. The Company Portal website is for end users.

prompt: Endpoint analytics shows a poor sign-in score. The administrator suspects third-party software that starts with Windows is keeping the CPU busy after the desktop appears. Which part of the startup performance report should be reviewed?

options.text: The Startup processes tab
The Model performance tab
The Restart frequency tab
The Work from anywhere report

explanation: The Startup processes tab lists processes that delay the time to a responsive desktop by keeping the CPU above 50% after the desktop renders, with device counts and delays. Model performance compares hardware models. Restart frequency analyses restart categories. Work from anywhere assesses cloud readiness.

prompt: Users complain that a line-of-business desktop app keeps crashing. The administrator wants to compare that app's crash counts and mean time to failure with other apps across the organization's Windows devices. Which endpoint analytics capability should be used?

options.text: Startup performance report
Remediations script packages
Application reliability report
Resource performance report

explanation: The application reliability report shows app-level metrics such as crash counts and mean time to failure across devices, which helps identify unreliable apps. With Advanced Analytics, the device timeline adds per-device detail. Startup performance measures boot and sign-in times. Remediations run scripts. Resource performance reports CPU and RAM pressure rather than app crashes.

prompt: An administrator wants to deploy Remediations to Microsoft Entra joined Windows devices. Which licence must the users of those devices have?

options.text: Windows Enterprise E3/E5, Education A3/A5, or VDA per user
Microsoft Intune Plan 1 with no other licence
Microsoft Entra ID P1 with no other licence
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 1

explanation: Remediations require users to have Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 (included in Microsoft 365 F3, E3 or E5), Windows Education A3 or A5, or Windows VDA per user, as well as Intune management. Intune Plan 1 alone isn't enough. Entra ID P1 and Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 don't include the required Windows licence.

prompt: A custom remediation package should fix a misconfigured registry value. The report shows the issue detected on many devices, but the remediation script never runs. The detection script writes 'Issue found' and ends with exit 0. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Turn on 'Run script in 64-bit PowerShell' for the package
Change the assignment schedule from daily to hourly
Turn on 'Enforce script signature check' for the package
End the detection script with exit 1 when the issue exists

explanation: The remediation script only runs when the detection script exits with code 1, which signals that the issue was found. Any other exit code, including 0, is treated as no issue. The PowerShell bitness, the schedule and signature checking don't change how the exit code triggers remediation.

prompt: The help desk suspects that one laptop model has frequent blue-screen crashes. In endpoint analytics, how can the administrator confirm whether Stop errors are a problem across the organization and then find the worst-affected devices?

options.text: Use the Work from anywhere report for each model
Use the Restart frequency tab, then the Device performance tab
Run Collect diagnostics on every laptop of that model
Review the Windows feature update report by model

explanation: The Restart frequency tab shows the 30-day count of restarts in each category, including Stop errors, and links to the Device performance tab sorted by restarts. The Model performance tab also shows average Stop errors per model. Work from anywhere doesn't track crashes. Collecting diagnostics from every device is slow and isn't an analytics view. Feature update reports track upgrades.

prompt: Each morning, an administrator wants to check in one place whether any configured Intune connectors (such as the Apple push certificate, Apple Business Manager tokens and the Defender for Endpoint connector) are unhealthy or close to expiring, and whether any active service incidents affect the tenant. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: Reports > Endpoint analytics
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
Devices > Monitor > Assignment failures
Tenant administration > Tenant status

explanation: Tenant status summarises connector health, based on last sync or expiry time, and shows service health incidents that affect the tenant along with message center posts. Endpoint analytics covers device performance. Entra sign-in logs record authentication. Assignment failures report policy deployment errors, not connector or service health.

prompt: A junior administrator should be able to read Intune message center posts on the Tenant status page to plan for upcoming changes, without receiving broader administrative rights. Which role meets this requirement?

options.text: Intune Administrator
Message Center Reader
Global Reader with Intune Administrator
Cloud Device Administrator

explanation: Viewing the Intune news feed in Tenant status requires the Message Center Reader role or the Service Support Administrator role. Message Center Reader is the least-privileged option here. Intune Administrator grants full Intune management rights. Combining Global Reader with Intune Administrator is even broader. Cloud Device Administrator manages device objects and doesn't target message center access.

prompt: When a device becomes noncompliant, the organization wants the user to receive an email explaining how to fix it, with the IT security mailbox copied, and a reminder email three days later if the device is still noncompliant. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Compliance policy 'Send email to end user' actions using a message template
A Conditional Access policy with a custom terms of use document
A Remediations script that sends email from each device
A Log Analytics alert rule on the Intune audit logs only

explanation: Compliance policies support actions for noncompliance. 'Send email to end user' uses a notification message template, can include additional recipients, and can be scheduled a number of days after noncompliance, so it can be added more than once for reminders. Terms of use doesn't send compliance emails. Sending mail from a device script is unreliable and unsupported for this. A Log Analytics alert alone doesn't email the affected end user with remediation steps.
